text: irene: Heads-up — accessibility + copy nit for the latency breakdown chart legend. Long model names get truncated to a single line with an ellipsis and the tooltip currently just repeats the full model name. That doesn't help when multiple variants share similar prefixes (e.g., "redwood-v2-large-8bit" vs "redwood-v2-large-4bit"). Thoughts on making the tooltip more actionable? josh: Good call. If the tooltip only shows the full name, it's hard to diff. Suggest adding a second line in the tooltip with a short descriptor like "quantized: 8-bit" or "region: us-west-2" when applicable. Keep the first line the friendly name. cal: Agree. Also for screen readers we should expose aria-label on each legend item that concatenates friendly name + descriptor, e.g., "Redwood v2 Large, quantized 8-bit". That way SR users get the distinguishing info without needing hover. priya: UX note: tooltips should stay compact (< 2 lines). Maybe show two lines: (1) Friendly name, (2) short context: "quantized • us-west-2 • 16 seq" (use middot separators). If we include multiple attributes, keep them short and consistent across items. mark: Mobile behavior: there is no hover. We surface the legend in a drawer; tapping an item should open a small popover with the two-line description and a "View model details" link. The popover copy should mirror the tooltip. Also watch button widths. irene: Proposed tooltip / sr strategy: - Visual tooltip (short): line1 = "Redwood v2 Large"; line2 = "8-bit quantized • us-west-2" - Screen reader aria-label on the legend button: "Redwood v2 Large, 8-bit quantized, region us-west-2, accounts for 12% latency" - Mobile tap popover: same as visual tooltip plus a small link: "View model details" -> /models/redwood-v2-large josh: Small copy nit: use natural phrasing for SRs, avoid punctuation-only lists. E.g., "Redwood v2 Large — 8-bit quantized, region us-west-2" reads better. For percent include actual number only if known (avoid rounding noise). cal: Implementation note: I'll expose data attributes: data-sr-text and data-tooltip-lines so we can compute SR text in the component. Example markup suggestion: ```html ``` priya: Also add an aria-describedby id that points to a visually-hidden node containing the percentage and an explanation like "part of overall latency breakdown" so SRs get context. Keep the hidden node concise: e.g., "12% of total query latency". mark: One more: when items are truncated we should provide an explicit "ellipsis aria-label": set title attr to the friendly name for browsers that show native tooltips, but rely on our custom tooltip for SR and mobile. Avoid duplicating content in the DOM for SEO/analytics. irene: Final copy and accessibility handoff (for the PR): Visual tooltip (max 2 lines): Line 1 (friendly): "Redwood v2 Large" Line 2 (context): "8-bit quantized • us-west-2" Screen reader aria-label (single sentence): "Redwood v2 Large — 8-bit quantized, region us-west-2. Represents 12% of total query latency." Mobile tap popover: - Title: "Redwood v2 Large" - Subtitle: "8-bit quantized • us-west-2" - Link: "View model details" -> /models/redwood-v2-large (opens panel) Implementation notes: - Add data attributes for building aria-labels and tooltips server-side. - Use aria-describedby to point SRs at a visually-hidden node with the percent line. - Keep tooltip copy compact; avoid repeating long model IDs. - Ensure focusable legend items (keyboard nav) and role=\"button\" or \"menuitem\" as appropriate. cal: I'll wire the attributes and share a small component example in the PR. I'll also check keyboard navigation and focus order. priya: Happy with the copy. For localization teams: provide templates for the two-line tooltip and SR sentence separately to avoid stacking translated strings. irene: Thanks all — I'll update Figma annotations and attach the accessibility checklist to the PR. :sparkles: design-bot: Copy + a11y note recorded — ticket #CI-9872.
